def: To tame; to subdue. [Obs. & R.] Sylvester.
One who does not tempt, or is not a tempter. [Obs.] Wyclif.
The state or quality of being inky; blackness.
A bag in which feed for a horse, ox, or the like, may befastened under the nose by a string passing over the head.
A receiver; the person or thing that receives; one to whom, orthat to which, anything is given or communicated; specifically, thereceiver of a still.

Not capable of expression or utterance in language; ineffable;unspeakable; indescribable; unutterable; as, inexpressible grief orpleasure. "Inexpressible grandeur." Blair.In orbs Of circuit inexpressible they stood. Milton.
In an essential manner or degree; in an indispensable degree;really; as, essentially different.
In a technical manner; according to the signification of termsas used in any art, business, or profession.
